fixes.explanation: Judah is where Jehoshaphat is king, and he's in this battle with Ahab. But the order doesn't name him. It says, "…except the king of Israel." Ahab is the king of Israel, so he's the one on the list.

True. The chariot commanders see Jehoshaphat and say, "Surely this is the king of Israel!" Then they turn to fight against him. They're doing what their king ordered, and they think they found their man.

Actually, they do make that call. The text says the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat and said, "Surely this is the king of Israel!" Then they turned to fight against him. They were sure they had their man.

False is right. When the chariot commanders saw that Jehoshaphat was not the king of Israel, they "…turned back from pursuing him." Their order was about the king of Israel, and this wasn't him. Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, got to breathe again.

The king of Aram is the one who gave the order about the king of Israel, but he's not the one hit. The text says the arrow "…struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor." That's Ahab. The passage never says the arrow hit the king of Aram.

Morning is too early. The text says "The battle raged throughout that day…" and Ahab was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans. Then "…that evening he died." The day had gone a long way before it ended.

True. As the sun was setting, a cry rang out in the army: "Every man to his own city, and every man to his own land!" The call is for the men to go back to their own cities and lands. It's a fitting end to a very long day.
